title: Navi AI Agent: Research Strategy for Generative AI
subtitle: Two bounded workstreams, three validated pain points, one repeatable benchmark

slides.title: Navi: Research Strategy for Generative AI in Business Spend Management
slides.standfirst: Directing research for an AI agent embedded across an enterprise platform — while stopping an open-ended AI mandate from consuming the entire research team.

bullets.text: Director of User Experience Research and Design
Two time-boxed workstreams: Opportunities and Components
Quantitative UEQ benchmark for an AI feature at Coupa

slides.notes: This is a research-leadership case as much as a research case. The interesting decision is structural: how to bound something that has no natural end.

slides.title: Heavy investment in generative AI, without evidence of where AI actually helped
slides.standfirst: The question was not whether the models worked. It was whether they resolved anything a procurement or finance professional was actually stuck on.

callout.text: An open-ended ML discovery effort of this size threatened to absorb the whole team's capacity and expand indefinitely, with no defined end state.

slides.notes: Two problems stacked: an evidence gap in the product, and a scoping failure waiting to happen in the function. The second one is what would have killed the first.

slides.title: Three recurring failure modes came out of the interviews
slides.standfirst: Named from customer interviews and thematic analysis, and taken straight to the roadmap.

cards.title: Credit confusion
cards.text: Users could not predict or understand what an AI interaction would cost them — so they hesitated before asking.

cards.title: Query issues
cards.text: Users did not know how to phrase a request the agent could actually act on, and had no way to learn.

cards.title: Product disconnect
cards.text: The agent felt bolted on rather than continuous with the workflow the user was already inside.

callout.lead: Note what none of these are
callout.text: None is a model quality problem. All three are experience problems, which is why they were invisible to the teams measuring model performance.

slides.notes: Credit confusion is the one that surprised people most: anxiety about burning credits changes behaviour before the model is ever invoked.

slides.title: One mandate, split into two things that could each finish
slides.standfirst: Strategic discovery and design validation ran in parallel, time-boxed, so neither absorbed the other.

figure.caption: Two bounded workstreams, each independently deliverable

slides.notes: The reason this works: each stream has its own deliverable and its own end date, so neither can quietly borrow the other's capacity.

slides.title: Opportunities — define the problem space, then go and watch

bullets.text: With customers, analysed thematically rather than tallied.
Planned with customers across diverse businesses, to see real-world AI usage rather than reported usage.
User anxiety around burning credits — a behaviour people do not report but do exhibit.

callout.text: Self-report on AI use is unreliable in both directions: people overstate how much they use it and understate how much they hesitate.

slides.notes: The credit-anxiety finding is the strongest argument for the observational component. It came from watching, not asking.

slides.title: Components — test the AI surfaces as interface, not as intelligence

bullets.text: How an AI-generated element announces itself as generated.
How a user asks, corrects, and overrules.
The assistant inside procurement scenario comparison, where the stakes are a real award decision.

slides.notes: Component testing is what fixes product disconnect. You cannot solve "it feels bolted on" at the model layer.

slides.title: Recommendation and evidence, in the same view
slides.standfirst: Navi presents cost-savings insights alongside the raw supplier data, so the user sees what was suggested and what it was suggested from.

figure.caption: In enterprise procurement, an unauditable recommendation is not usable

slides.notes: In a domain where decisions are audited, hiding the evidence does not build trust in the AI — it disqualifies it.

slides.title: "Better" is not a research finding until it has a baseline
slides.standfirst: A Navi UEQ instrument was layered over both workstreams, producing the first repeatable quantitative benchmark for AI feature quality at Coupa.

callout.text: The next release can be compared to this one. Without that, every AI improvement claim is an assertion, and every regression is invisible.

slides.notes: This is the piece that connects to the wider research-operations work: UEQ was already being stood up as a programme, so the AI feature inherited a method rather than inventing one.

slides.title: Six scales, applied the same way every time
slides.standfirst: The User Experience Questionnaire measures across six dimensions — which is what makes an AI feature comparable to a non-AI one, and to itself six months later.

items.label: Attractiveness
items.detail: Overall impression: do users like it at all

items.label: Perspicuity
items.detail: Is it easy to become familiar with and to understand

items.label: Efficiency
items.detail: Can users solve their task without unnecessary effort

items.label: Dependability
items.detail: Do users feel in control of the interaction

items.label: Stimulation
items.detail: Is it motivating and interesting to use

items.label: Novelty
items.detail: Is it innovative and creative — the scale AI features over-index on

figure.caption: Dependability is the scale that matters most for an agent that acts on your behalf

slides.notes: If asked why UEQ rather than a bespoke survey: comparability across products and across time, and it was already the standard instrument in the function.

slides.title: Pay AI: eleven interviews to a live Early Adopter Program
slides.standfirst: The same model applied to autonomous invoice selection — bounded scope, specific decision, clear handoff.

bullets.text: Which invoice batches are low-risk enough to select autonomously?
Eleven customer interviews, analysed for selection criteria rather than sentiment.
Defined low-risk batch selection criteria, and an Early Adopter Program built on them.

figure.caption: Bounded question, bounded study, shipped outcome

slides.notes: Eleven interviews is a small study that produced a product decision. Worth saying explicitly — scope discipline is the theme of the whole deck.

slides.title: Generative AI discovery has no natural stopping point, so you have to build one
slides.standfirst: The primary challenge was structural, not methodological: protecting scope and capacity by splitting an open mandate into two bounded, independently deliverable streams — while still producing evidence rigorous enough to redirect an executive roadmap.
slides.notes: For a research-leadership audience this is the whole talk. Rigour that bankrupts the team is not rigour.
